summary: iter95t backend + frontend testing for foreman Harmonogram (schedule). Created 16 pytest tests covering auth, /api/budget/my-schedule scoping (admin/foreman), PATCH /api/budget/tasks/{id} role-based field whitelist, future-date validation, clear_actual_end_date flag, cross-site denial, and direct invocation of cron_schedule_notify_foremen(). All 16 PASSED. Frontend smoke via Playwright confirmed foreman login flow (3 testid'd inputs), push-gate dismissal, foreman-tab-schedule tab as FIRST tab in WorkerDashboard, empty state copy 'Brak zadań na najbliższe 14 dni', and ?tab=schedule deep-link activating Harmonogram.
critical_code_review_comments: Two collections track sites: finance_budowy (used everywhere) vs construction_sites (used for budowa_name lookup in /budget/my-schedule). If a finance_budowa exists but no matching construction_sites doc, budowa_name will be null. Consider unifying or falling back to finance_budowy when name missing.
/app/backend/routes/budget.py exceeds 1500+ lines - should be split (lines/positions/progress/tasks/schedule submodules) per >700-line guideline.

Pre-existing test-data issue (noted by main agent): Roman.assigned_sites IDs (67c1465e-c4be-4d29-b08b-37094d04b193, 33fc3748-7bbf-4c7e-a193-cbf4b1d9e6f7) do NOT match real construction_sites IDs (Castorama=67c1465e-5f53-4c03-837a-e0d536517cc8, LEBA=33fc3748-2a2e-4715-bd21-22e00af824de). Tests still pass because admin can create tasks directly on those orphan IDs, but production foreman won't see real-site tasks. Not iter95t bug, but fix the seed data so foreman testing works realistically.
